source.title: Interpreting Key Mechanisms of Factual Recall in Transformer-Based Language Models
source.authors: Ang Lv; Kai-Yi Zhang; Yuhan Chen; Yulong Wang; Li-Feng Liu; Ji-Rong Wen; Jian Xie; Rui Yan

page_placements.theme: Backup and suppression heads: how they are located and what triggers them

record.tranche_reason: The paper does not test downstream self-repair. It speculates in its limitations that multiple circuit paths may compensate when one pathway is patched, and says this may relate to the Hydra effect.
record.gate_note: The paper's head-patching experiments identify influential heads or examine blocking negative heads; they do not compare an ablated component's direct effect with its total effect or measure downstream restoration. The negative-head blocking result is recorded as a related finding, not evidence for any listed version.
record.test_reason: The paper studies factual-recall mechanisms (mover heads, MLP 'activation', a final-layer anti-overconfidence mechanism). It never compares an ablated component's direct effect with its total effect, and never measures downstream restoration after ablation. Self-repair appears only as speculation in the Limitations (Appendix J), which says another pathway 'could compensate' and may relate to the Hydra effect. The final-layer suppression of the correct token resembles V2's late-MLP erasure. But the authors do not test whether this erasure shrinks when earlier components are ablated, and it is not framed as self-repair.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that factual recall works as follows: task-specific mover heads pass the topic token, MLPs act as an 'activation' that amplifies or erases head outputs, and a deep MLP's intercept steers toward the answer. A universal final-layer anti-overconfidence mechanism suppresses correct predictions and can be mitigated. Self-repair is mentioned only speculatively in the limitations.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses activation/path patching and head-output replacement in factual-recall experiments, not the original self-repair measurement comparing component direct and total effects.

fits_no_version.finding: The final-layer MLP (with layer-11 attention heads attending to the first token) suppresses the correct answer Y across GPT-2, OPT-1.3B and Llama-2. Subtracting the regression intercept, plus attention masking, raised the zero-shot P(Y) from 5.53% to 25.93% in GPT-2 small.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Late layers universally downweight confident correct predictions (anti-overconfidence), independent of any ablation. This is related to, but distinct from, V2's ablation-dependent erasure.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean-patching negative heads L10H7 and L11H10 only slightly alleviates suppression of X; Y stays low.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In GPT-2 small country-capital prompts, the negative heads suppress X rather than Y.

record.problems: The study does not measure self-repair, direct-versus-total ablation effects, or restoration after ablation. The related head-blocking outcome is described qualitatively and shown in a figure.
record.rows_left_out: The path-patching results in Figures 3, 5, 13, 16, and 17 identify influential heads in factual recall; they do not report downstream compensation or restoration and are not included as self-repair results.

untested.parts: Whole-layer ablation and later-layer compensation are not measured.
Final MLP suppression of Y is observed, but there is no test of erasure shrinking under earlier ablation.
There is no head-ablation compensation measure, either on general text or on tasks.
Variability and overcorrection of compensation are not measured.
Negative heads and the final-LayerNorm/MLP anti-overconfidence mechanism are described, but not as carriers of self-repair.
Mean ablation is used, but self-repair is not measured under it.
There is only speculation that patching one pathway may be futile; no test.

record.verdict_notes: There are no verdicts because no version is tested. The anti-overconfidence result (Figs 6, 9, 15, 17, 19) is topically adjacent to V2 but involves no ablation-conditioned erasure. It is left as a fits_no_version finding with no rows, since the record does not capture it as a row.

versions.untested_parts: Layer ablation followed by compensation in later attention layers.
Late-MLP counterbalancing and its change under earlier-component ablation.
Head-ablation compensation on the full output distribution across general text, model families, and sizes.
Prompt-level variability and overcorrection in compensation.
Self-repair under on-distribution ablations such as mean or resample ablation.
Whether ablation-based importance scores misstate component function because of self-repair.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Replaced the outputs of negative heads L10H7 and L11H10 with their average activations at the country-name position to block out country identity.
rows.measure: Probabilities of X and Y across layers
rows.value: Text states that blocking the heads slightly alleviates suppression of X at layer 10, but suppression remains strong at layer 11; Y increases slightly but remains relatively stable and low overall.
rows.note: The intervention and probability effects are reported, but the result does not measure downstream compensation or restoration of the original prediction.
rows.check: The row is correctly unlinked. It mean-patches negative heads and reports X/Y probabilities across layers. It does not measure whether downstream components compensate. The description is qualitative, figure only (Fig. 7).

source_check.locator_found: Section 3.1; Appendix A.3, Figure 7: blocking L10H7 and L11H10 mitigates X suppression at layer 10; suppression remains strong at layer 11. Y increases slightly but remains low.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Appendix J speculates that collaborative circuit paths could compensate for patched pathways and relates this possibility to the Hydra effect.

tranche.reason: The study measures factual-recall mechanisms and prediction suppression, without testing compensation after ablation or using self-repair as a tool.

source_check.notes: Final-layer suppression is measured, but its reduction following earlier-component ablation is untested. The qualitative Figure 7 result establishes no self-repair verdict.
